description: I'm Ahmet, a Biomedical Engineering student at Yildiz Technical University and founder of HYBRIDLAB. I have experience in robotics, embedded systems, 3D design, and STEM education, including technical leadership in FRC teams. I enjoy turning ideas into working prototypes. I'm looking for teammates interested in software, electronics, design, or research to combine our skills, learn from each other, and build practical solutions together.
summary:
HYBRIDLAB Lunar Greenhouse is an interactive STEM education platform that combines physical hydroponic cultivation with a NASA-inspired space agriculture simulation.

The system features a transparent 1.9-liter growing reservoir with five planting positions, an air pump for root aeration, and a 7-inch ESP32-S3 touchscreen. Students can grow real plants, observe root development through the transparent container, and record plant growth, water pH, and electrical conductivity (EC).

Alongside the physical growing system, students can explore a virtual lunar greenhouse with two experimental chambers. They can independently adjust pH, EC, light intensity, light duration, light spectrum, and temperature, then compare simulated plant growth through interactive graphs and scientific explanations.

The project integrates authentic NASA research references, including the VEG-04 experiments aboard the International Space Station, connecting students' experiments to real space agriculture research while clearly distinguishing simulated predictions from NASA measurements.

By combining hands-on plant cultivation, interactive experimentation, and space science education in one compact device, HYBRIDLAB makes complex scientific concepts accessible and encourages critical thinking, environmental awareness, and interest in sustainable food production on Earth and beyond.
details:
Project Details — HYBRIDLAB Lunar Greenhouse

Project Overview

HYBRIDLAB Lunar Greenhouse is an interactive educational platform that connects real-world hydroponic agriculture with virtual space exploration. Our goal is to make scientific experimentation accessible, engaging, and understandable by allowing students to grow real plants while exploring the challenges of cultivating food beyond Earth.

Unlike conventional educational simulations, our project integrates a physical growing environment with an independent, NASA-inspired digital experimentation platform.

Physical Hydroponic System

The physical system consists of a transparent 1.9-liter growing reservoir with five planting positions, an air pump for oxygenating the nutrient solution, and a 7-inch ESP32-S3 touchscreen interface.

Students can plant seeds, monitor germination, observe root development through the transparent reservoir, and document changes in plant growth. The touchscreen provides interactive guidance and allows users to record pH, electrical conductivity (EC), and visual observations.

This hands-on experience introduces students to plant biology, nutrient management, sustainable agriculture, and hydroponic cultivation.

NASA-Inspired Lunar Greenhouse Simulation

The digital simulation introduces two independent greenhouse chambers: Greenhouse A (Control) and Greenhouse B (Experimental).

Students can select plants such as lettuce, dwarf tomatoes, and strawberries, then investigate how different environmental factors influence their development.

The adjustable variables include:

  • Nutrient solution pH and electrical conductivity (EC)
  • Photosynthetic light intensity (PPFD)
  • Daily light exposure duration
  • Red, blue, and green light composition
  • Greenhouse temperature

Students formulate hypotheses, modify experimental conditions, and compare plant development using visual growth indicators, interactive graphs, estimated biomass, and explanatory results.

An accelerated simulation allows students to explore up to 60 virtual growing days in approximately 30 seconds, making long-term biological processes accessible during classroom activities.

Integration of NASA Research

Our project incorporates scientific references from NASA's space agriculture research, particularly the VEG-04 experiments conducted aboard the International Space Station.

The simulation includes documented experimental lighting parameters and introduces students to investigations involving light spectra, plant development, and harvesting strategies.

Additional educational references explore related NASA research, including VEG-05 dwarf tomato experiments and controlled-environment plant cultivation studies.

Students encounter research-based educational questions and explanations connecting their experiments to actual scientific investigations.

Importantly, the simulated growth predictions are generated by an educational mathematical model and are clearly distinguished from real NASA experimental measurements.

Technology and Development Tools

The platform was developed using an ESP32-S3 microcontroller and an 800 × 480 capacitive touchscreen.

Our main technologies include:

  • C programming language for embedded software and simulation logic
  • ESP-IDF for ESP32-S3 firmware development
  • LVGL for touchscreen interfaces, animations, and interactive visualizations
  • FreeRTOS for task management and responsive operation
  • NVS and SPIFFS for persistent settings, experiment records, and graphical assets
  • Fusion 360 and 3D printing for mechanical design and physical prototyping

The physical growing system uses transparent components to support direct observation, while the digital simulation operates locally on the microcontroller without requiring continuous internet access.

Educational Innovation and Intended Impact

The project's main innovation is combining a tangible biological experiment with an accelerated virtual scientific environment in one compact educational device.

Students can experience the patience and observation required for real plant cultivation while exploring alternative environmental conditions through simulation.

The platform also incorporates gamification, including scientific challenges, virtual harvesting, resource management, and greenhouse upgrades, to encourage exploration and sustained engagement.

During development, we prioritized educational accessibility, compact hardware design, intuitive touchscreen interaction, offline functionality, and scientific transparency.

Our intended impact is to strengthen scientific literacy, experimental thinking, environmental awareness, and interest in space exploration.

By connecting NASA's research with everyday classroom experimentation, HYBRIDLAB Lunar Greenhouse helps students understand how innovations in space agriculture can inspire more sustainable approaches to food production on Earth and support future human exploration beyond our planet.
